text:
anya: quick thread — thinking about canary windowing for onboarding benches. we see long fat-tail latency spikes in a small subset of models; how do we fold that into acceptance heuristics without exploding cost?

sam: +1 this has been annoying. current canary window is 10m which smooths most noise but misses rare 95/99 spikes.

mike: idea — two-phase: short fast window (2-5m) to catch regressions that affect p50/p90, then an extended tail window (1-2h) sampling at low qps to capture fat-tail behavior.

olivia: sampling at low qps is fine but we need deterministic seeds for replay. otherwise we get variability when re-running bench buckets.

anya: agree. propose config shape: 
```
canary_window_short: 5m
canary_window_tail: 90m
tail_sample_rate: 0.05  # 5% of requests routed to tail sampler
replay_seed: <sha256(prompt-set)>
```

sam: that looks reasonable. question: where do we store tail samples? bench storage is expensive if we keep raw inputs. maybe keep hashes + minimal metadata and replay generator to recreate prompts.

mike: yes store hashes + a small replay manifest (prompt_id, seed) and link to S3 bucket for full text, TTL 30 days by default.

olivia: also add a gating rule: fail canary only if both short-window and tail-window show regressed error or latency above threshold. prevents noisy one-off failures from blocking rollout.

anya: sounds good. edge case: model variants that have very bursty token generation (e.g., reprompt loops) — the tail sampler might under-sample those because qps-based sampling misses burst severity.

sam: we can add a burst detector during short window: if variance(token_rate) > X then force-tail-sample that session. basically an on-demand promotion.

mike: implementation note — the admission pipeline currently assumes fixed window durations in the orchestrator. we'll need to make windows pluggable and non-blocking (trigger tail sampler async).

olivia: operational question: how do we show tail metrics in console? not just aggregated percentiles but a small histogram and example sessions. ops wants quick triage artifacts.

anya: UI proposal: in run details show 3 panes: short-window summary (p50/p90/p99), tail-histogram (log-binned), and 3 example sessions from tail sampler with full token logs. link to replay manifest.

sam: +1. also add a rollback heuristic: if tail p99 increases by > 2x and short p90 increases by >20% then auto-fallback to previous model for first 5m.

mike: we should be careful with auto-fallback flapping. add cooldown per app and exponential backoff on rollouts.

olivia: deploy-bot: can you create a patch to make canary windows configurable per-model in the onboarding pipeline? we want defaults but override per model. :slightly_smiling_face:

deploy-bot: @olivia created task I-4827: make canary windows configurable + tail sampler plumbing. CI job will run linter + integration smoke.

anya: before we close, action items:
- mike: prototype async tail sampler + replay manifest (ETA 3d)
- sam: spec rollback heuristics and cooldown (ETA 2d)
- olivia: UX mockups for 3-pane run detail (ETA EOW)
- anya: write short RFC that captures interface (window config + tail sampling contract) (ETA 4d)

sam: one more: add metrics tags so billing can attribute tail sampling cost to team/model (we don't want hidden cost surprises).

mike: yep will add metric tags and a debug flag to increase tail_sample_rate for stress tests.

olivia: cool. if no objections i'll mark this done and we can sync on the RFC review.

anya: no objections from me. thanks all :rocket:
